item.title: Four types of House races to watch on election night to know how it might go
item.description:
There's a lot at stake for energy in the midterms, from the fate of the bipartisan permitting deal to the growing backlash against data centers and electricity prices. Why it matters: The results could spotlight which energy topics resonate with voters — and which have become political liabilities. Gasoline and diesel prices have been big on the campaign trail, offering a chance to see how much voter frustration over energy costs matters at the ballot box. Data center politics: There are sharp differences between the parties, even though data centers aren't especially popular with either party's slate of candidates. Why it matters: The pace of the AI buildout affects power demand and emissions. item.title: Russian bombing kills 31 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
item.description:
The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people. Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post. FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

item.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
item.description:
North Korea is denying being involved in the hack on Binance. Korea Summit Press Pool/Getty Images North Korea denies involvement in Binance's $6 billion crypto theft. Kim Yo-jong accused the US of using cybercrime allegations to harm North Korea's global reputation. Binance detected a $6.3 billion breach and said it would cover losses. North Korea has denied that it was behind the $6.3 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Binance , calling the FBI's allegation a "grave political provocation." In a Tuesday statement, Kim Yo-jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said: "The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a 'cyber criminal state,' claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization 'supported' by the DPRK was involved in the incident." The statement was carried by the state-run Korean Central News Agency and republished by South Korea's Yonhap News…

item.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as midterm elections start
item.description:
The United States has conducted defensive strikes on some Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said Monday, on the eve of crucial midterm elections. The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on U.S. gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress. item.title: Trump’s Closing Argument Is About Algae
item.description:
Will undecided voters in states such as Alaska and Michigan base their ballot decisions Tuesday on President Donald Trump’s fountain repairs in Washington, DC? If so, Trump’s 47-minute appearance on Monday afternoon at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool would make sense. But polls sh0w voters are worried about high prices , corruption , and Trump’s war with Iran , not DC algae blooms. And the president’s use of his final scheduled appearance before the midterms to talk about pipe replacements looks like the bizarre self-indulgence of a guy utterly uninterested in the problems of regular Americans. item.title: What Do Libertarians Have To Gain From the Midterms?
item.description:
This week, editors Peter Suderman , Katherine Mangu-Ward , Nick Gillespie , and Matt Welch discuss what the midterm elections could mean for libertarians. They debate whether a Democratic victory might help curb President Donald Trump's executive power and why Republicans may struggle to learn from their mistakes. The conversation then turns to races in Ohio, Alaska, and Michigan that reveal growing tensions within both parties. The editors then examine how much power Democrats would actually have if they retake Congress, particularly when it comes to Trump's tariffs and the war with Iran. They also weigh the value of congressional investigations against the risk of more political grandstanding. Finally, a listener's question about gerrymandering leads to a discussion of electoral reform and the possibility of expanding the House of Representatives. 0:00—What the midterms mean for…

item.title: Why South Africa's local elections matter
item.description:
High crime rates and a lack of basic services are causing concern among many of South Africa’s 29 million registered voters. Water shortages and unreliable electricity supplies have also become symbols of municipal failures, angering voters and eroding support for the ruling African National Congress. The municipal elections on November 4 will offer a glimpse into whether these frustrations are shifting political loyalties.

item.description:
We cannot let the billionaire class take unprecedented risks with our future America is a divided country in crisis. Despite the sunny economic forecast coming from the Trump administration, millions of Americans are struggling to find and keep jobs, getting crushed under the rising cost of living, and losing health insurance when they need it the most. Meanwhile, via corporate consolidation and political corruption, the billionaire class is getting richer faster than ever before: a 40% increase in wealth in just the last two years.
